market_summary: US stocks slipped about 1% intraday Nov 17 (SPY -1.1%, QQQ -1.1%) ahead of Nvidia's Q3 FY27 print after the close, with consensus at $109.3B revenue and $101.8B data-centre. The 10-yr Treasury sat at 5.12% on Nov 16, still above 5% and keeping AI build financing costly. AI capex signals stay firm on the ground: H100 rents at $3.08/hr and B200 at $6.94/hr near highs, while DDR5 spot is flat at highs. China risk rose with US moves to curb remote access to AI chips; oil is range-bound near its 200-day average, and gas-turbine deliveries for data-centre power continue.

AXOS.reason: Down 0.9%; no news. 8.8x forward with 4.64% margin is cheap.

LDI.reason: Down 1.9%; no forward earnings and two brokers halved targets last week.

STRIPE.reason: No new round or tender reported since Nov 13.

OPENAI.reason: No new round or tender reported since Nov 13; Anthropic IPO will reset AI comps.

headlines: Chips slide again on new China curbs: TSMC -3.5%, Micron -3%, Alibaba -3.9%; S&P and Nasdaq ETFs about -1%.
Nvidia Q3 tonight after US close = Wed morning AEDT; first print under interim CEO Kress.
Street wants about $109B revenue, $102B data-centre from Nvidia; GPU rents still near highs at $3.08/hr.
Anthropic IPO prices Wed after US close (Thu morning AEDT); book reported about 6x covered.
